items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: I’ve had situations where I’ve been commissioned to do things for the Joe Henderson big band CD

ctx.x: Hampton composition but we want a new thing. Where do you start with something like that?

Well I’ve been asked the question many times how do you start to approach either a composition or an arrangement. You have to start actually just be getting an idea of what it is that whoever you’re going to do it for, wants. And then to let it develop in a natural way. And the feeling for it, and the idea of it in your mind, let it develop in a natural way. So if you say you want a composition and you have a certain instrumentation, that instrumentation alone can inspire you a place to start. Once you get a…
Does the individual you’re writing for shape the way you write also?

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I joined the band. When I joined the band, McCoy Tyner was there. Joe Henderson, Bill Hardman, Junie Booth, and Art.

ctx.x: ’62 is the first Slide Hampton octet. What happens between ’59 and ’62?
Art Blakey. I joined Art Blakey’s band.
This is well before you made that Killer Joe record with him.
